description: Guide a student to implement an RSI mean-reversion strategy with asymmetric entry/exit thresholds and stop-loss across the full Binance futures universe on LEAN. Unlike I02's simple crossover, this task requires per-symbol entry price tracking, long/short state machines, stop-loss logic, and risk-based position sizing that limits exposure per symbol. At universe scale, the student must manage ~100 independent position state machines concurrently.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I want to test a buy-low-sell-high strategy with stop-losses on all the crypto futures in my dataset — about 100 of them. How do I manage all those positions at once on LEAN?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I'm implementing a universe-wide RSI mean-reversion strategy on LEAN. Each symbol needs its own state machine for long/short/flat with stop-loss tracking. How do I structure this for ~100 symbols?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I need a production-grade mean-reversion strategy on LEAN across ~100 crypto futures with proper risk management. What's the cleanest architecture?
student_openings.fullstack_practitioner: I need to implement an RSI mean-reversion strategy with asymmetric. I've done similar work in Python before — let's focus on getting the architecture and edge cases right.
student_openings.developer_crossover: I need to implement an RSI mean-reversion strategy with asymmetric. I can handle the code, but I don't understand the financial logic behind it. What should this do and why?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a LEAN C# algorithm that (1) subscribes to ~100 symbols and creates per-symbol RSI indicators, (2) implements RSI entry/exit and fixed stop-loss logic independently per symbol, (3) manages per-symbol position state (flat/long/short) with entry price tracking, (4) implements risk-based position sizing (5% per position, capped total — 5% avoids LEAN's MinimumOrderMarginPortfolioPercentage silent rejection at smaller sizes), (5) tags exit reasons (RSI signal vs stop-loss) in the trade log, and (6) produces universe-level aggregated statistics. Per-symbol trades for 10 reference symbols should match the ground-truth.
required_capabilities: Manage per-symbol RSI indicators and position state at scale (~100 symbols)
Implement asymmetric entry/exit logic with per-symbol state machine
Track entry prices per symbol and compute stop-loss conditions
Handle long/short positions without overlap, independently per symbol
Implement risk-based position sizing (5% per symbol via SetHoldings)
Tag exit reasons and produce universe-level aggregated statistics
ground_truth.termination_criteria: The tutor has completed the following steps with computational evidence (not just verbal discussion): (1) Showed C# code for a universe-wide RSI mean-reversion strategy with per-symbol entry/exit logic and stop-loss handling. (2) Presented backtest results with specific numerical values such as total return, Sharpe ratio, or number of trades. (3) Showed trade log output with entry/exit records that include exit reason tagging such as signal exit versus stop-loss. (4) Responded to the student's follow-up about the implementation or results with additional explanation, code refinement, or analysis beyond the initial demonstration. Once all four steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
